mainEntity.name: What is a father-in-law suite and what does it usually include?

acceptedAnswer.text: A father-in-law suite is a self-contained living area created within, attached to, or detached from a main home. It typically includes a dedicated bedroom, a full bathroom, a living area, and either a kitchenette or full kitchen to give a family member privacy and autonomy. When planning this space, a key decision factor is choosing between building a brand-new home addition, converting an existing area like a garage, or reconfiguring interior rooms. Attached additions share structural elements and HVAC connections with the main house, whereas converting existing space may lower framing needs but requires updating insulation, drywall, and utility access. Establishing your relative's mobility needs and daily routines early determines the ideal layout and entry placement.
